schema_notes.change: Per-surface arithmetic.safe is a string drawn from arithmetic_status_values (SAFE, PARTIAL, NOT_ASSESSED, NOT_SAFE) instead of a boolean, so a reader that tested the old boolean form has to migrate. anchor_grammar, arithmetic_status_values and schema_notes were added in the same version, and every string in every surface is now anchor-checked.

Anchors now name symbols and must resolve to exactly one definition in the named file. Numeric line anchors were removed because their evidence rotted after unrelated insertions; Python methods use Class.method when needed, while C macros/static const objects and Python module constants can anchor non-function definitions.

scope: Public, user-supplied runtime and supported offline-tooling parser boundaries for ISO/SFO, encrypted PSP containers, ELF/PRX, every native and Python JSON consumer (title manifest, runtime package, library, cache/identity, font cache, input profile, player settings, and package-builder documents), XB/GIM, PSMF/MPEG/H.264/ATRAC, PGF, and the supported tooling readers (title runtime config, staging manifests, sweep reports, flight-recorder bundles, performance summaries, the publication profile, and frame-dump PPM files). Corpora are source-owned synthetic inputs; private inputs/evidence are outside scope.

surfaces.boundary: Private package/cache manifest and title-input-identity JSON
surfaces.max_input: tools/nk_core/package_cache.py:MAX_CACHE_JSON_BYTES = 1048576 bytes per externally supplied JSON artifact (package.json, completion-manifest.json, title-input-identity.json). The ceiling is enforced by a bounded read of at most MAX+1 bytes through one open handle (fstat and reads share the descriptor; the extra byte catches growth), never a whole-file read. Valid data at the exact limit is accepted. build-report.json is the one artifact whose bulk scales with the analysed title (one record per AOT gap, unsupported instruction and analysis diagnostic), and a measured flagship report is about 1.3 MB, so it reads through tools/nk_core/package_cache.py:read_build_report_json under its own ceilings: MAX_BUILD_REPORT_JSON_BYTES = 4194304, MAX_BUILD_REPORT_JSON_NODES = MAX_BUILD_REPORT_JSON_MEMBERS = MAX_BUILD_REPORT_JSON_ITEMS = 262144. The planner refuses to write a report above that byte ceiling (tools/title_codegen_plan.py:_build_report_text). The separate public title-manifest route in tools/nk_cli.py uses the title-manifest reader's 262144-byte default.
surfaces.tables_nesting: Duplicate keys are rejected by name at any depth. Pre-parse structural scan before json.loads: MAX_CACHE_JSON_DEPTH = 32 nesting levels, MAX_CACHE_JSON_MEMBERS = 16384 object members, MAX_CACHE_JSON_ITEMS = 16384 comma separators (the legacy MAX_CACHE_JSON_ITEMS name), MAX_CACHE_JSON_NODES = 65536 structural nodes, so hostile nesting or bulk fails at a named ceiling before recursing inside the standard parser. For build-report.json the member and separator ceilings are raised to the node ceiling because those counts bind first (a 1.3 MB report of AOT-gap records reaches 16384 members while still under 65536 nodes); each member and each separator is at least one structural node, so they stay bounds that cannot reject a document the node ceiling accepted. Post-parse per-record object validation precedes field access.
surfaces.allocation_time: JSON memory/time is bounded by the byte and structural ceilings; build-report.json uses its own larger ceilings (4194304 bytes, 262144 nodes, members and separators) while every other package/cache artifact keeps 1048576 bytes and 65536 nodes. Decimal integers have a local 4300-digit ceiling checked before conversion, independent of Python's optional process-wide guard; a stricter host guard yields a named BoundedJsonError. NaN, Infinity and floats that overflow to infinity are rejected; supported floats must be finite. RecursionError inside json.loads is contained to the named BoundedJsonError. Artifact digests stream in 1 MiB blocks. Rejection messages bound the untrusted text they quote: an externally supplied key, field name, or scalar is echoed only as a short prefix, and an untrusted name list only as a fixed-size sample, so a hostile artifact cannot inflate a diagnosis (or a log that records it) by its own size.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: Validation is read-only; package promotion stages and rejects invalid copies. Malformed or hostile input raises the named BoundedJsonError (or the entry point's named failure embedding it) -- never AttributeError, TypeError, RecursionError, or UnicodeDecodeError. Nothing is truncated silently. Rejection messages bound the untrusted text they quote: an externally supplied key, field name, or scalar is echoed only as a short prefix, and an untrusted name list only as a fixed-size sample, so a hostile artifact cannot inflate a diagnosis (or a log that records it) by its own size.
surfaces.harness: tools/test_package_cache.py; tools/test_nk_core.py; tools/test_parse_fuzz.py validates inventory anchors and claims
surfaces.gap: Resource ceilings, deterministic hostile-input corpus, and named controlled errors are now executable behavior on production entry points. No seeded-mutation loop or sanitizer target for this Python parser route.
malformed_input_coverage: Contract corruption, duplicate keys, invalid cache identity/artifact path, digest mismatch and incomplete package cases.

Bounded-input regression: exactly-at-limit valid JSON accepted; one-byte-over limit rejected; excessive nesting (100k levels) and member/node counts rejected with named errors; duplicate keys rejected; malformed UTF-8 rejected; wrong top-level type rejected; growth during read cannot bypass the ceiling.

Build-report ceiling regression: a synthetic report in the planner's AOT-gap record shape at the measured flagship size (about 1.3 MB, over the shared 1 MiB byte ceiling) validates cleanly through validate_package_cache; a report exactly at MAX_BUILD_REPORT_JSON_BYTES is accepted and one byte over is rejected with the named byte-limit error; package.json still fails at the shared 1048576-byte ceiling; the report reader's 262144-node ceiling is enforced and named while the shared 65536-node ceiling still applies to every other artifact; and the planner refuses to serialize a report above the reader's byte ceiling.

Numeric regression: NaN/Infinity and float overflow reject on the production reader; oversized integers reject before conversion with bounded named diagnoses; integers at the local digit ceiling and ordinary signed integer/float values retain their types.

Bounded-diagnostics regression: no rejection message on any of these routes echoes attacker-supplied bulk data; an oversized key, unknown field name, non-integer schema_version, or repeated disc_id is quoted only as a short prefix and an oversized unknown-field list only as a fixed-size sample, while the rejection itself stays a named controlled error. The structural node count is a true lower bound for every scalar and trailing-string document.
resource_gaps: No seeded-mutation or sanitizer campaign for this Python JSON route.

surfaces.max_input: GameLibrary.load and nk_cli library routes enforce 1048576 bytes and a 4096-record upper bound. The shared reader uses a bounded MAX+1 read on one descriptor and rejects growth. The byte and structural limits apply independently of record count; GameLibrary.save validates the temporary output with GameLibrary.load before replacing an existing library.
surfaces.tables_nesting: Both routes reject duplicate keys and apply the 32-level pre-parse depth ceiling and shared library budgets: 57347 object members, 61443 comma separators, and 118792 structural nodes. Unknown root/record fields, per-record object types, and non-negative integer counts are checked by GameLibrary.load only. nk_cli checks the integer schema version, games list and record count; its bring-up records have a different field schema.
surfaces.allocation_time: Read memory is bounded by the byte ceiling; decoded structure is bounded by the structural ceilings and the record limit; RecursionError inside json.loads is contained to the named controlled ValueError. Rejection messages bound the untrusted text they quote: an externally supplied key, field name, or scalar is echoed only as a short prefix, and an untrusted name list only as a fixed-size sample, so a hostile artifact cannot inflate a diagnosis (or a log that records it) by its own size.
surfaces.failure_atomicity: GameLibrary.load returns a new library only after every record validates. Each GameLibrary.save owns a unique temporary file in the destination directory, validates it with the same reader before atomic replacement and cleans up only that file on failure. Overlapping saves cannot overwrite/unlink one another's temporary files; the last completed replacement wins, without merging concurrent record edits. nk_cli checks the post-update record count, serialized UTF-8 byte count and structural budgets before atomic replacement; rejection preserves the previous library. The existing save formats are retained. nk_cli has its separate bring-up record schema; compatibility with GameLibrary records is not established. Rejection messages bound untrusted echoed text. No silent truncation occurs.
malformed_input_coverage: GameLibrary save/load round trips preserve all fields, including 1200 fully populated records. A byte-limit failure during save preserves the previous library and removes temporary output.
Deterministically interleaved production saves complete with separate temporary files and leave no owned temporary output; saving preserves another writer's existing library.json.tmp checkpoint.

nk_cli reads and updates a 4096-record library. Appending beyond the record limit or writing beyond the byte limit rejects without replacing existing bytes. The writer rejects boolean schema versions.
The shared numeric parser rejects nonfinite library timestamps and integers above 4300 digits with controlled errors; no NaN or infinity enters loaded records.

Shared bounded-reader coverage on GameLibrary.load and nk_cli._load_library_entry: exact byte limit accepted, one byte over rejected, excessive nesting rejected, duplicate JSON keys rejected, malformed UTF-8 rejected and wrong top-level type rejected. Each route checks its games-list type and record count.

GameLibrary.load-specific coverage: null/scalar/list records, invalid field types, unknown root/record fields, repeated disc IDs, missing games and unsupported schema versions reject with controlled errors. These record-field rejection claims do not apply to nk_cli bring-up records.

Bounded-diagnostics coverage limits echoed attacker text; structural counters cover bare scalars and trailing strings. The aggregate comma-separator diagnosis includes object separators and does not claim to count array elements exclusively.

The native font-cache manifest reader, the package-builder prerequisite and install-receipt readers, the sweep-report reader, and the publication profile loader have no direct test; their CI coverage is indirect or absent.

status_definition.COVERED: Deterministic malformed/seeded regression evidence is present in the named CI path; this does not imply sanitizer, coverage-guided fuzz, or issue acceptance.
status_definition.PARTIAL: Some source-backed bounds/tests exist, with one or more declared resource, execution, or sanitizer gaps.
status_definition.GAP: A material resource-limit, malformed-input mutation, or validation-coverage gap remains.

anchor_grammar.path: a repo-relative path (it carries a directory separator) that must exist in the tree; a bare filename in prose such as manifest.json names a product document and is not an anchor
anchor_grammar.path:symbol: the symbol must resolve to exactly one definition in that file; Python methods may use Class.method, and C #define/static const objects plus Python module-level assignments are supported definitions
anchor_grammar.line-number anchors: rejected: line numbers, line-plus-symbol, and line-at-function forms are not evidence and cannot be used
anchor_grammar.coverage: every string in every surface and in the document preamble is scanned for anchors, so a runner sentence, a resource gap, or a campaign note is checked the same as an entry
